ledger.note: 958: Boso I is the first count of La Marche. The page: 'La Marche first appeared as a separate fief about the middle of the 10th century', with Boso I count of La Marche and Périgord 958-988. The extent is the page's: 'approximately corresponding to the modern département of Creuse and the northern half of Haute Vienne'. [Reviewer eu-10-x, 2026-10-25] counterpart changed from kingdom-of-france (dossier 987-1792) to west-franks (843-989), the kingdom in 958.

1308: the childless Count Guy dies and the crown seizes the county. 'With the death of the childless Count Guy in 1308, his possessions in La Marche were seized by' the king (the House of Lusignan had held it since the 12th century, page text without a year).
1314: the king makes La Marche an appanage for his youngest son. 'In 1314, the king made La Marche an appanage for his youngest son the Prince, afterwards Charles IV.'

1327: La Marche passes to the House of Bourbon. 'Several years later in 1327, La Marche passed into the hands of the House of Bourbon.' (the page's list has Charles's exchange with Louis of Bourbon in 1322).
1435: the House of Armagnac takes La Marche. 'The family of Armagnac held it from 1435 to 1477, when it reverted to the Bourbons.'

1477: Louis XI confiscates the lands of Jacques d'Armagnac and La Marche reverts to the Bourbons. 'In 1477, Jacques was convicted of treason and his territories were confiscated by Louis XI of France.' The page has the county revert to the Bourbons in the same year; the sentences do not say who held it between.

notes:
Written for eu-10-x from one page (County of La Marche); the page gives no capital, no area and no towns. The state is the county as one region, Creuse plus Haute-Vienne (the page says the northern half of Haute-Vienne, drawn whole here), from 958 to 1526; its holders change (Lusignan in the 12th century; the crown in 1308; the prince Charles 1314; Bourbon 1327; Armagnac 1435-1477; Bourbon again; the crown 1527) and each change is a rename event (the royal-domain-of-france dossier carries the gains and losses). The page does not date the passage to Lusignan, the 13th-century enlargement, or the Bourbon holdings of 1477-1527 beyond 'Charles III, Duke of Bourbon 1505-1525'. It gives 1314 for the apanage and 1327 for Bourbon; 1322 for the exchange with Louis of Bourbon appears only in the list.
The Crown lands page (royal-domain-of-france) dates 'Angoulême, Fougères, Lusignan purchased from Yolande of Lusignan' to 1308; this page calls 1308 a seizure on the death of Count Guy, so Angoulême and La Marche are different counties and the purchases differ. Capital: Guéret is a map dot only (not on the page). | fx-32 F215: the northern half of Haute-Vienne is now drawn (polygon north of 45.9 N) instead of the whole department, as the page says; Limoges is outside the county.
